title: Competitive feature diffusion & supplier sourcing tracker
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Purpose: Build a repeatable playbook and artifact set that tracks how competitive model features, packaging/bundles, and licensing shifts diffuse through the market and create procurement triggers for Redwood. Scope: 1) a 2D heatmap of feature diffusion across vendor/model families (capability vector vs. time), 2) a supplier sourcing trigger catalog linked to signal thresholds, 3) a lightweight dashboard that surfaces upward momentum or feature parity events, and 4) automated Slack alerts for procurement/PM when triggers fire. Why: rapid vendor feature diffusion (e.g., lower-cost quantized variants, integrated retrieval plugins, function-calling enhancements) can create surprise churn/rate/capacity risk for our customers and procurement planning. This ticket is focused on the PM-side taxonomy, scoring rubric, proof-of-concept heatmap, and definition of procurement triggers; engineering and data infra tickets will follow for automation and ingestion.
success_criteria: A documented taxonomy of 18 feature signals and 5 capability axes (format: CSV + commentary)
Prototype heatmap (CSV + Metabase/Grafana dashboard) showing time-series diffusion for 10 vendor/model families
Sourcing trigger catalog with 6 actionable entries (e.g., price delta, feature parity, closed-source licensing change) and recommended procurement response
Runbook for signal validation and false-positive mitigation (linked to test prompt suite)
Stakeholder signoff from Procurement, Applied ML, and Platform PMs
deliverables: Procurement trigger catalog (with thresholds and response playbooks)
Alerting spec for Slack + Ops channel
One-pager for GTM/partnerships teams summarizing strategic risk vectors
approach: 1) Run a 6-week reconnaissance combining automated scraping of vendor release notes, marketplace price feeds, GitHub commit/issue signal harvesting, and curated customer-reported feature sightings. 2) Normalize signals into capability axes (e.g., inference cost per 1k tokens, quantization availability, function-calling parity, embeddings-stability metrics, multimodal pipelines). 3) Score diffusion velocity per model family and compute an adoption momentum metric. 4) Hand-validate top 30 signal events with SME interviews. 5) Populate dashboard and review with Procurement and Applied ML before automating ingestion.
timeline: Week 1 (Mar 1-7): finalize taxonomy, identify 12 vendor families, prototype scraping pipelines
Week 2 (Mar 8-14): collect historical 90-day signals, compute diffusion velocity, initial heatmap draft
Week 3 (Mar 15-21): SME validation, refine scoring thresholds, draft procurement triggers
Week 4 (Mar 22-28): dashboard build, stakeholder demos, iterate
Week 5 (Mar 29-31): finalize artifacts, handoff engineering tickets for automation
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: noisy/misleading release-note signals -> Mitigation: require 2 independent corroborating signals (marketplace price, GitHub change, or customer report)
Risk: legal/licensing ambiguity on vendor announcements -> Mitigation: flag for Legal review and classify as 'unverified legal change' in the catalog
Risk: dashboard scope creep -> Mitigation: focus first on a 10-family POC and the highest-impact triggers only
Risk: data ingestion infra workblocks automation -> Mitigation: deliver heatmap CSV and manual ingestion runbook for short-term use
